It has 2 sections of different diameter molded in to the flexible hose attachment end. Presumably, this accomodates different sized hose barbs. Fortunately, I found a brass connector with both dameters and hose clamped everything together. Very strong connection. But, very time consuming to find that nonstandard connector. That also goes for the cutlery drawer but it works great too! You can use the traditional rack.The Zeolite drying system is excellent. Don't rush it. It's a natural system and consumes no power at all.Bosch has a good reputation for a reason and we are very pleased with our decision. thanks to our daughter for recommending Bosch.

Comments (English): [ Good, not great. ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher is certainly above average in terms of visual appeal and overall function, however it is not, in my opinion, a high end dishwasher in terms of performance. With every load I have to rinse or rewash a few dishes, which was never needed with my previous comparable Bosch dishwasher. Also, the dishwasher does not clean dishes that are in the corners at all, and the plastic pieces that hold each rack attachment in place do not stay put. I have to reset several of the adjustments between each wash because the plastic clips are not strong enough to stay in place. Overall, the plastic pieces do not seem to be sturdy and seem to be low quality. Also, the third rack is not spacious enough to fit the dishes that made that third rack so handy in my previous dishwasher. It is so tight to the top of the dishwasher, only flatware and Tupperware lids can fit, which greatly reduces the advantage of having a third rack. Also though a minor issue, it advertises 44db sound, however it is noticeably louder than my previous Bosch dishwasher with the same 44 db rating. Overall it is a good dishwasher, but it is nowhere near the quality of the Bosch dishwasher that it appears to have been designed to rival.

Sentence (English): We had an old Kenmore dishwasher that finally died after over 22 years.
Comments (English): [ Would be great if it actually dried the dishes. ] || ---------------- || We had an old Kenmore dishwasher that finally died after over 22 years. I consulted Consumer Reports which gave this dishwasher a great rating and it had the features I was looking for, some of which are hard to find, like the time remaining in a cycle. What I love about this dishwasher: huge capacity, very quiet, shows time remaining in cycle, cleans dishes well. Unfortunately it just does not dry the dishes. After a heated dry cycle (even extended dry, and even with rinse aid) the inside of the dishwasher is soaking wet. So if you've run it overnight and it's been closed a while, not only are the dishes wet, but it starts to smell mildewy. What I currently have to do is pop the door open slightly as soon as the dry cycle is done, and that helps - BUT - that means I have to be around right when the cycle finishes. And even then, I still have to either hand-dry or air-dry a lot of items. I'm not talking about a bit of water on top of plastics - that is fairly normal. I'm talking drops of water on the insides of cups and bowls. The water also pools on the lids of the silverware basket, so as you pull the silverware out, it touches the water and gets wet. So I have to leave the tops open. A dishwasher is supposed to make your life easier, and this does not. I could hand-wash and dry everything quicker. Our extremely old dishwasher had no problem washing and completely drying dishes in about 90 minutes. (The "quick wash" was even faster! ). Here, the quick wash and dry is about an hour and 40 minutes (which would be fine if it actually dried). Regular and deep clean cycles are around 3 and 4 hours which I find ridiculous (and again, dishes won't be dry after all that). I am very disappointed and wish I had chosen something else. If I could return this, I would. It's a shame, because everything else about it is great. If a 22-year-old dishwasher could get the job done (without rinse aid even), then there is no reason a dishwasher today can't do the same thing. Sentence (English): I bought this dishwasher in 2022.
Comments (English): [ Year 2 Issues ] || ---------------- || I bought this dishwasher in 2022. Selection was a little sparse due to supply chain issues. The Good: This has a stainless steel liner, a third row and decent reviews. It's quiet and does a good job cleaning the dishes, and we run it several times a week. The Bad: I noticed the clear plastic cover on the control panel along the top of the door had started to separate (become unglued). Over the next few months the display led and buttons started to malfunction. I took the door and control panel off and found that water had seeped into the circuit board and damaged it. I was able to order a new control cover and new circuit board and replace them. I'm disappointed with the quality with the failure in only two years of normal use. I'm glad I was able to repair it, but it should not have failed after two years. I'm attaching pictures of the control cover and circuit board. Not a cheap fix, but relatively easy to find parts and do the repair.

Sentence (English): I'm going to list every pro and con, then explain why this dishwasher deserves a 5 star rating from me and doesn't deserve an overall 3.9 star rating .
Comments (English): [ Don't base your decision based on the bad reviews! ] || ---------------- || I'm going to list every pro and con, then explain why this dishwasher deserves a 5 star rating from me and doesn't deserve an overall 3.9 star rating . First, It has a shorter depth than the average American dishwasher which allows it to be evenly flush with the cabinets creating a aesthetically pleasing look, Second, it is quiet (based on some negative reviews they mentioned it was loud but i dont believe that to be true and must have been installation issue). Third, built in water softener, if you live in an area with super hard water this dishwasher has a water softener built in, if you have hard water than you know the struggle and the damage it causes on your glass cups. Its embarrassing giving a guest a cloudy glass not because the water is dirty or your dish is dirty but because your dishwasher water has caused a permanent etching in the glass. Fourth, it cleans and dry dishes well, I was happily surprised with how dry things were. Fifth, the top rack is adjustable in height. Lastly, stainless steel tub and operating instructions are very user friendly. There are of course Cons, first the height doesnt meet the standard American height for countertops, it can be raised but still won't reach the standard 24inchs (but it's barely noticable). Second, with it's depth and height being a little less than the average its probably won't fit a few dishes (literally maybe a few dishes). So, why give it 5 stars, because as someone who generally uses reviews to determine if i should buy something and read it's loud, and leaks, but I still get it and it's actually a pretty decent dishwasher for the price and quality. Give it a shot is all I am saying.

If you are going to keep it in that position, then angle it outwards to give you sight of the controls.

So, even though we had a built-in dishwasher when we moved into our new house, I didn't use it. My friends told me it was so convenient to have a dishwasher, so I used it a couple of times. It was loud and felt unsettling, so I stopped using it afterward. Then, when we started working together, I started feeling stressed about cleaning up after work or having guests over. Then I found this dishwasher! They said bigger is better, so I removed the 14-inch built-in dishwasher from our house and installed it. I use the top compartment for cutlery and cutlery, and the bottom for dishes, bulky items, and tall items. It washes well and is incredibly convenient! I just remove some large items, add a bottle of all-in-one detergent, and it runs smoothly, quieting down the noise and cleaning up. I'm very satisfied :) It's definitely quieter than my old one!

Sentence (English): Full disclosure we have yet to really read the manual.
Comments (English): [ Third Rack is the BEST ] || ---------------- || Full disclosure we have yet to really read the manual. So, it took a while for us to realize that the right-side tiny light on the outside is "blue for washing", "red for drying" and "clear for done" - wished it had a countdown clock on the outside like our last machine. The line on the left is just a vent. That said. I LOVE the TOP THIRD RACK - it is amazing. It is life changing. Why did this take so long to be "invented"? With four people packing Tupperware lunches and dinners, we always had stuff left in the sink when our last dishwasher was full. No more. Our cereal bowls, Tupperware and some mugs can fit on top rack along with the big spoons and spatulas - I don't put greasy stuff on the very top. The top dishes are already fairly clean since we rinse well before putting in machine so it doesn't get clogged with food. This extra rack makes all the difference and the other racks are very spacious and have a great layout - same with silverware basket with two side compartments with doors to hold small stuff inside. I would recommend this to anyone who has a lot of dishes to wash! I use the "quick wash" - 1 hour 48 min! which I think is as quick as it goes - doesn't really seem to have too many options (which is ok for us because the dishes are clean) and "heat dry" - sometimes the plastic isn't dry but I think that is a universal issue for all machines. Glad we bought this machine.

Sentence (English): Dishwasher technology has improved a great deal in the last decade!
Comments (English): [ Bosch is better than I even expected ] || ---------------- || Dishwasher technology has improved a great deal in the last decade! There are fair, good and best choices when it comes to service and reliability. There are features that are gimmicks and features on the market that actually work well and add value. I chose Bosch after reading many reviews that tout the excellence of the machine and the value for the money spent. I did not think I could ever be excited about a dishwasher. After all, it just cleans the dishes right? What I failed to realize, was that the little annoyances with dishwasher of the past were no longer an issue, until I purchased my Bosch 800 series! This machine is German technology at its finest! My dishes have never been cleaner or dryer (including plastics). Here are the features that I valued more once I experiened the benefit: 1. The top rack for flatware and other utensils. I thought this was a gimmick until I used it one time after I entertained for the holidays! It allows you to have more surface area to clean things that would otherwise take up space in the lower racks. The adjustable wings that lower to allow slightly larger items works well.2. The adjustable height middle rack. You can lower one side to that wine glasses that are taller, do not hit, or you can lower the entire rack in a multitude of heights. This is a game changer especially if you have taller, more delicate items because it saves space on the lower rack and still allows you to have a more gentle spray for them. 3. You can some verticle prongs in strategic areas allowing items like pots to fit or thicker bowls to slide in perfectly. I use this feature almost evey time.4. You can adjust the spray on the bottum to spray more intensely on items that have tougher grime. (I have never had to use this feature because on "auto" setting, everything has come out spotless.4. Auto setting automatically detects when your dishes are clean or if they are not using internal sensors. It works! 5. Crystal Dry: The dishwasher has a compartment that contains volcanic minerals that aid in removing moisture from the air. This is a Bosch only feature, not available on any other brand of dishwasher and an example of Bosche superior engineering. My dishes have never been dryer because I use this setting every time. Even plastic items come out dry or dryer. That is one feature I really appreciate. No hand drying of wet plastic items! 6. There is no heating element which saves energy costs. This dishwasher has a "sanitize" setting that superheats the water. In combination with "Crystal Dry" the dishes come out sanitized and dry. It is simply amazing. 7. The controls are hidden but there is a red light that shines on the floor until the cycle is complete. Great idea! 8. 42 decibels! My kitchen is practically in my TV room. The dishwasher is practically silent even in the kitchen.9. Split silverware holders: There are two holders so that one can be removed. Once one is removed, you can lower the veritle "in between" prongs and place pots and bans in the rack with more available space. I have never had to use both silverware holders since the top third rack will hold all silverware if necessary. 10. Pots that have hard water stains come out like new.There are several choices on the market for dishwashers of this price point and a few that cost much more. There is no need to spend a penny more since the Bosche performs flawlessly, quietly and reliably. The results speak for themsevles. Am I excited about a dishwasher? Yes, I am because it is one less problem in life I have to deal with. The Bosch 800 makes my life a little bit easier and that is worth a lot!

I could not ask for more. Now my husband has no excuse not to take part in "doing the dishes".

Sentence (English): The Bosch 300 series dishwasher really does a great job of getting dishes clean and sparkilng.
Comments (English): [ A bit disappointing ] || ---------------- || The Bosch 300 series dishwasher really does a great job of getting dishes clean and sparkilng. Drying is acceptable but some may not like it. Water pooled on top of glasses and bowls that have a recessed underside remains. I have not tried the extra dry option or any other option available only through the app. I have been using it for about 1 month and I am still trying to figure out how to load bigger items like dow bowls and mixing bowls without losing all the space on the top rack. The spacing between the tines is too narrow or too large and their angle too steep to easily hold these items vertical in the bottom rack. I manage, but I imagine it would be hard to fit everything a medium/large family or cooking enthusiasts use in a day. I love the 3rd rack to hold knives and bigger ustensils. The silverware basket is really small, but extra silverware can beput in the 3rd rack. Regarding the all important noise level, it is so much better than my old one! Still, it makes a loud hum when first filling up with water that I dislike (hence, the disappointment) and sometimes the spray arm to the upper rack makes an annoying whining sound when operating. That was worse when I had the upper rack tilted on one side. I'm not sure if any of this is normal or if I have particularly sensitive hearing. Other than that, it is pretty quiet. Overall I am satisfied with the performance of this machine. I did not install it myself, so I can't say how easy this process is. But I anticipate a lot of hassle and cursing when/if a problem arises because all the connections are in the back and the unit has to be pulled out to check/repair.

Comments (English): [ It ok at best, until it wasn't. ] || ---------------- || Purchased this in March of 2022 to replace my old Kitchenaid dishwasher I had for 20 years. I was such a fan of that dishwasher, I thought after 20 years they could only be better, right? Wrooong. First off, I could throw ANYTHING in my old dishwasher and it always came out clean. I would specifically leave dishes out to test it and they always came out sparkling. Not this one, at all. I did all the recommended steps in the beginning to essentially prime it, but nothing helped. I have to run it on the toughest setting if I leave the least amount of food on my dishes, let alone dried food. I don't know if I've ran a load where there isn't some white residue left on at least a few of my dishes.

Sentence (English): When I was looking for a replacement for my 20 year old Maytag, I didn't consider Bosch until I read the Consumer Reports.
Comments (English): [ Wow! ] || ---------------- || When I was looking for a replacement for my 20 year old Maytag, I didn't consider Bosch until I read the Consumer Reports. All I can say is WOW! You guys have outdone yourselves. It is so quiet, I have to check to make sure it is running. I get clean dishes and NO standing water on things. I'm still not sure what the 3rd tray is for though. I put my plastic cookware up there.(Spatulas, etc.) The installation was a rather difficult due to the installers not being familiar with the new models but, eventually got worked out after 5 visits. If you want a dishwasher that REALLY cleans your dishes and doesn't leave water standing on them, is so quiet you wonder if it's working and does look good. This is the one. My one issue is the door. When it is open, it is about 3-4 inches off the floor so you can roll out the bottom rack. For those of us with bad backs, this does create an issue. Thankfully, I can still get down there but, my wife is unable. We moved the silverware basket up to the middle rack and only put big things in the bottom rack. Anyway, thank you. I love it.

Sentence (English): Dishwasher technology has improved a great deal in the last decade!
Comments (English): [ Bosch is better than I even expected ] || ---------------- || Dishwasher technology has improved a great deal in the last decade! There are fair, good and best choices when it comes to service and reliability. There are features that are gimmicks and features on the market that actually work well and add value. I chose Bosch after reading many reviews that tout the excellence of the machine and the value for the money spent. I did not think I could ever be excited about a dishwasher. After all, it just cleans the dishes right? What I failed to realize, was that the little annoyances with dishwasher of the past were no longer an issue, until I purchased my Bosch 800 series! This machine is German technology at its finest! My dishes have never been cleaner or dryer (including plastics). Here are the features that I valued more once I experiened the benefit: 1. The top rack for flatware and other utensils. I thought this was a gimmick until I used it one time after I entertained for the holidays! It allows you to have more surface area to clean things that would otherwise take up space in the lower racks. The adjustable wings that lower to allow slightly larger items works well. 2. The adjustable height middle rack. You can lower one side to that wine glasses that are taller, do not hit, or you can lower the entire rack in a multitude of heights. This is a game changer especially if you have taller, more delicate items because it saves space on the lower rack and still allows you to have a more gentle spray for them. 3. You can some verticle prongs in strategic areas allowing items like pots to fit or thicker bowls to slide in perfectly. I use this feature almost evey time. 4. You can adjust the spray on the bottum to spray more intensely on items that have tougher grime. (I have never had to use this feature because on "auto" setting, everything has come out spotless. 4. Auto setting automatically detects when your dishes are clean or if they are not using internal sensors. It works! 5. Crystal Dry: The dishwasher has a compartment that contains volcanic minerals that aid in removing moisture from the air. This is a Bosch only feature, not available on any other brand of dishwasher and an example of Bosche superior engineering. My dishes have never been dryer because I use this setting every time. Even plastic items come out dry or dryer. That is one feature I really appreciate. No hand drying of wet plastic items! 6. There is no heating element which saves energy costs. This dishwasher has a "sanitize" setting that superheats the water. In combination with "Crystal Dry" the dishes come out sanitized and dry. It is simply amazing. 7. The controls are hidden but there is a red light that shines on the floor until the cycle is complete. Great idea! 8. 42 decibels! My kitchen is practically in my TV room. The dishwasher is practically silent even in the kitchen. 9. Split silverware holders: There are two holders so that one can be removed. Once one is removed, you can lower the veritle "in between" prongs and place pots and bans in the rack with more available space. I have never had to use both silverware holders since the top third rack will hold all silverware if necessary. 10. Pots that have hard water stains come out like new. There are several choices on the market for dishwashers of this price point and a few that cost much more. There is no need to spend a penny more since the Bosche performs flawlessly, quietly and reliably. The results speak for themsevles. Am I excited about a dishwasher? Yes, I am because it is one less problem in life I have to deal with. The Bosch 800 makes my life a little bit easier and that is worth a lot!

Sentence (English): I read the reviews.
Comments (English): [ Incredibly hard to install without leaking ] || ---------------- || I read the reviews. I knew what I was getting myself into. And still I thought: “surely, I can install this filter without it leaking! ” Oh how wrong I was. I am astounded by how easy it is for the filter to be installed with significant leaking, and how little difference there is between “correctly” installing and “incorrectly” installing. I am fortunate that enough people have posted about the leaking problem that I at least knew to look for it. So after my first attempt yielded heavy flow into my cheese drawer (which I pompously neglected to empty a priori), I quickly stopped and removed the filter. (And thankfully Samsung designed this so there is no flow when the filter is removed). Second attempt: massive leak. I finally stopped to re-review the other reviews here and attempted a third time. Leak. So I watched some YouTube videos. Well apparently fourth time is the try because - voila! - magically, no leak! I could not tell you what I did differently from the other three times. The only tiny nuanced difference – maybe – is that I pointed the filter arrow as little as possible below 9:00 (just past 90 degrees from locked position) to allow the filter to push into the slot, then pushed in gently while turning clockwise to 12:00 locked position. i.e., don't orient the filter arrow towards the unlock symbol at bottom left of the filter slot. 2 stars because it does seem to work if you can get it installed correctly (and it does appear to be possible). Good luck.

I am astounded by how easy it is for the filter to be installed with significant leaking, and how little difference there is between “correctly” installing and “incorrectly” installing. I am fortunate that enough people have posted about the leaking problem that I at least knew to look for it. So after my first attempt yielded heavy flow into my cheese drawer (which I pompously neglected to empty a priori), I quickly stopped and removed the filter. (And thankfully Samsung designed this so there is no flow when the filter is removed). Second attempt: massive leak. I finally stopped to re-review the other reviews here and attempted a third time. Leak. So I watched some YouTube videos. Well apparently fourth time is the try because - voila! - magically,  no leak! I could not tell you what I did differently from the other three times. The only tiny nuanced difference – maybe – is that I pointed the filter arrow as little as possible below 9:00 (just past 90 degrees from locked position) to allow the filter to push into the slot, then pushed in gently while turning clockwise to 12:00 locked position. i.e., don’t orient the filter arrow towards the unlock symbol at bottom left of the filter slot. 2 stars because it does seem to work if you can get it installed correctly (and it does appear to be possible). Good luck.

Sentence (English): This is a review of a product I purchased with my own money.
Comments (English): [ Dishwasher installation is possible without a hitch! ] || ---------------- || This is a review of a product I purchased with my own money. <If you only want to see the review of the dishwasher product, please just look at the marked section! Please only read from the beginning if you want to see the drill-free installation process.> First of all, since I live in a public rental housing apartment, the dishwasher installation process was very tricky. The first Samsung technician who visited told me to return the product, saying that they couldn't drill because it was natural marble. It’s not like this is Banpo Xi or anything; there’s no way it’s natural marble. I even confirmed with the construction company that it was artificial marble, but the technician gave me the absurd answer that the construction company was mistaken. ;;. I filed a complaint with Coupang and Samsung, and eventually, another professional technician came to reinstall it. However, another problem arose this time. There is a designated drilling location set by the management center, but they said drilling is impossible in this area because the stone is too thick. Then I remembered seeing a review on Coupang about someone having installed it without drilling. So, I asked them not to return it and just leave the product behind. If you search 'dishwasher automatic water supply' on the internet, there is a title titled "Connection Kit Hose Included." A shopping site will appear, and you can purchase the product that suits you there. You can buy it for just under 30,000 won. The installation process is not difficult either; as shown in the second photo, you simply need to plug it into the middle of the sink hose. If you have the hose with you before the dishwasher installation, technicians may install it for you. However, those who are strict about the book will not do it. The technician I met also told me that I had to handle the no-drilling installation myself. Also, the white line attached to the sink hose might look unsightly, but for me, the satisfaction of being able to use a dishwasher itself is so great that it outweighs that. It truly changes my quality of life. Below is a review of the product. It is huge. I roughly measured the length shown on the product detail page before receiving it, but in reality, it seems even bigger than that. The front-to-back width is really extensive. For my first attempt, I put in the dishes left over from making kimchi fried rice. There was a side plate that required 3-4 washes by hand to remove the grease, but the dishwasher lady cleaned it perfectly in just one standard wash. Spoons, tongs, scissors, and everything else came out squeaky clean, and even delivery containers were washed immediately. It gets clean enough to be recycled. I cut a bottle of the famous "FrX" detergent in half and put it in. It washed everything perfectly clean without a single water stain, even without using rinse aid. I was sure there would be residue on the glass cups, but even after checking thoroughly, there isn't a single water stain. The noise level is really low. I was worried because I saw a few reviews saying it was loud, but the sound is just loud enough to let you know the machine is running. If you leave it running and go into a room, you can barely hear it. When stacking items upside down, frying pans fit, and quite a few large plates fit in as well. It seems like the perfect capacity for a two-person household. It has an automatic door opening feature that opens automatically when the cycle is finished. Since this product does not support SmartThings, this is an essential feature. There is a lot of condensation inside after the wash is complete, but if you leave the door wide open, it will dry neatly after about two hours, so you can close it then. I am so happy that my stress has decreased so much since installing the dishwasher. Buying late only leads to regret. I recommend adding it to your cart and waiting for a discount before buying.

I am so happy that my stress has decreased so much since installing the dishwasher. Buying late only leads to regret. Since it can be installed easily without drilling, you should definitely buy a dishwasher! I purchased it in the late 30s range, including card benefits. I recommend adding it to your cart and waiting for a discount before buying.

Comments (English): [ Bosch is better than I even expected ] || ---------------- || Dishwasher technology has improved a great deal in the last decade! There are fair, good and best choices when it comes to service and reliability. There are features that are gimmicks and features on the market that actually work well and add value. I chose Bosch after reading many reviews that tout the excellence of the machine and the value for the money spent. I did not think I could ever be excited about a dishwasher. After all, it just cleans the dishes right? What I failed to realize, was that the little annoyances with dishwasher of the past were no longer an issue, until I purchased my Bosch 800 series! This machine is German technology at its finest! My dishes have never been cleaner or dryer (including plastics). Here are the features that I valued more once I experiened the benefit: . 1. The top rack for flatware and other utensils. I thought this was a gimmick until I used it one time after I entertained for the holidays! It allows you to have more surface area to clean things that would otherwise take up space in the lower racks. The adjustable wings that lower to allow slightly larger items works well. 2. The adjustable height middle rack. You can lower one side to that wine glasses that are taller, do not hit, or you can lower the entire rack in a multitude of heights. This is a game changer especially if you have taller, more delicate items because it saves space on the lower rack and still allows you to have a more gentle spray for them. 3. You can some verticle prongs in strategic areas allowing items like pots to fit or thicker bowls to slide in perfectly. I use this feature almost evey time. 4. You can adjust the spray on the bottum to spray more intensely on items that have tougher grime. (I have never had to use this feature because on "auto" setting, everything has come out spotless. 4. Auto setting automatically detects when your dishes are clean or if they are not using internal sensors. It works! 5. Crystal Dry: The dishwasher has a compartment that contains volcanic minerals that aid in removing moisture from the air. This is a Bosch only feature, not available on any other brand of dishwasher and an example of Bosche superior engineering. My dishes have never been dryer because I use this setting every time. Even plastic items come out dry or dryer. That is one feature I really appreciate. No hand drying of wet plastic items! 6. There is no heating element which saves energy costs. This dishwasher has a "sanitize" setting that superheats the water. In combination with "Crystal Dry" the dishes come out sanitized and dry. It is simply amazing. 7. The controls are hidden but there is a red light that shines on the floor until the cycle is complete. Great idea! 8. 42 decibels! My kitchen is practically in my TV room. The dishwasher is practically silent even in the kitchen. 9. Split silverware holders: There are two holders so that one can be removed. Once one is removed, you can lower the veritle "in between" prongs and place pots and bans in the rack with more available space. I have never had to use both silverware holders since the top third rack will hold all silverware if necessary. 10. Pots that have hard water stains come out like new. There are several choices on the market for dishwashers of this price point and a few that cost much more. There is no need to spend a penny more since the Bosche performs flawlessly, quietly and reliably. The results speak for themsevles. Am I excited about a dishwasher? Yes, I am because it is one less problem in life I have to deal with. The Bosch 800 makes my life a little bit easier and that is worth a lot!

The slots are almost so small to be a joke. The door requires some force to open and if you don't have your hand in the door open slot correctly you can cause the front door panel to buckle slightly as you open the door. Other than that: Washer is very quiet and does a good job of cleaning.

Sentence (English): My previous dishwasher was a Miele G21xx class and my review is based on a comparison with that 10 year old unit.
Comments (English): [ Good value on a quiet dishwasher ] || ---------------- || My previous dishwasher was a Miele G21xx class and my review is based on a comparison with that 10 year old unit. I purchased the Whirlpool dishwasher WDTA50SAKZ without seeing it in a showroom and instead just looked at the photos of the unit on a website. I purchased this dishwasher due to the likelihood of available parts 10 years down the road compared to the Miele. The latter where the parts are expensive and hard to find without reaching out to Miele head office. The Whirlpool dishwasher is surprisingly quieter than I expected. It's on par with the Miele unit as one can easily have a quiet conversation while near the dishwasher and the sounds from the dishwasher isn't obtrusive. Installation of the unit was pretty straight forward. The run time in normal cycle is 3 hours when heat is used to dry the content. I'm surprised at how often I have caked on food on the fork/spoons that I place on the top rack. I've taken out the utensil basket from the bottom rack so that I can have more room. Bottom rack cleaning capability are good and I rarely have to deal with caked on food even in frying pans/pots. Middle rack cleaning also meets my expectations. The height clearance on both the bottom and middle rack are greater than what I was experiencing on the Miele. In the bottom rack, the gaps in between the plates are significantly larger in the Whirlpool compared to the Miele. Top rack utensil holding capacity is about 30-40% less than on a Miele. So, I need to be creative on how to place the utensils. There is no 'flat' area on the top rack so the capacity to hold sharp objects such as 8"-12" knives isn't really possible. So, I have to be careful when placing and pulling them out. Yeah. some would say that knives shouldn't be placed in the dishwasher but I've been doing it for the past 25+ years and I'm still using my original 30+ year Henckels. Cleaning wise, the top rack isn't as good as the Miele. I would say that I see stuck on food on one or two utensils about half the time I use the dishwasher. I wish this dishwasher had a large drip pan under the wash basin. The Bosch and Miele would likely catch any future drips and signal an alert. I'm impressed with the Bosch since it's designed to even catch a leaky seal at the interface of the water intake hose and the dishwasher. The Whirlpool unit doesn't appear to have anywhere near such a comprehensive leak detection assembly. Overall, I feel that the dishwasher doesn't clean as well and I can't seem to load as much into it as the Miele that I had used for so long. Price wise though, the Whirlpool is almost 60% less so it's a compromise and so it's unfair to truly compare the two. I would still recommend the Whirlpool for those that are looking for a sub $1000CDN unit.

Comments (English): [ Love the inside. Controls a bit confusing ] || ---------------- || The short version is that I love the inside of this dishwasher, but not a big fan of the outside or the programming.Here is the long version. Starting with the inside, this may be the best designed interior I have seen. The tines that hold plates and bowls are very well spaced, and they ALL are adjustable so that they can be lowered out of the way depending on what you happen to be washing. The adjustable heigh middle rack has fold out cup racks for keeping stemware in place. Just make sure that both sides of the rack are adjusted to the same height so that the water connection at the back attaches properly when you push the rack in. The middle height setting is generally perfect for me, allowing my flexible cutting boards on the bottom to clear the middle spray arm, while letting me put taller glassware in the middle rack. I have taken advantage of the rack height adjustability, but only rarely. I really like the top rack and the fact that the left side also has a height adjustment for deeper items. I generally use that adjusted to the deepest setting and almost always have that rack at least half full. The shallow side sees less use, but I like that I can put small items there that I used to always have to hand wash, and don't worry about them falling through. With all the possible adjustments and efficient placement of the tines I feel like I can get almost twice in this machine as my previous dishwasher. The only real ding I have for the inside design is the handle on the silverware basket. It is wide and interferes with a decent portion of the available space. The good news is that with a butter knife you can depress the clips that hold it in place on each side and remove it. Just a little less convenient not having a handle but gives much more space to load silverware. I never had a silverware basket with slots, but this one works great and I really like the feature. My mom got a new dishwasher after me of a different brand and their silverware basket seems less efficient with the spacing. Another inside feature to mention is the fact that there is no heating element. I have some mixed feelings here. This means that plastic that may fall below won't get melted on a hot burner, and this is probably more gentle on my dishes and plasticware, so that's good. They use heat from the wash process that is trapped by your dishes to affect the drying. Initially ALL of my dishes were coming out completely wet. This unit REQUIRES that you use a rinse aid to help with the drying process. Using that does make my China and silverware come out dry, and plastics will have some water but significantly less than before. They do allow you to adjust the amount of rinse aid added, and I have had good luck with the lowest setting. I don't like the idea of having extra chemicals from the rinse aid added to the surface of my dishes, but this seems to be the current trend and I can at least set the amount to low. Cascade rinse aid says that if it gets in your mouth you should rinse your mouth, drink a glass of water and call poison control. LG did include an “extra dry” option, but that adds over an hour to the process and though it's been a while since I tried using that with no rinse aid, it seems like my dishes were still wet. I do use the “night dry” which uses a fan to assist with drying once the wash is complete, but doesn't change the run time. It simply operates for a while after the run time has ended. Opening the door during “night dry” cancels any additional fan time.Now for the outside. The appearance is fine. It's pretty plain. The controls are on top rather than the front, which I have mixed feelings about. They are easy access while the door is open and give a sleek appearance with the door closed, but that means that when in use you have no idea what program was selected or how much time is left on the cycle since the countdown timer is also located on top. I would prefer to have some information on the front (especially the timer and maybe a confirmation of the cycle settings) but this is somewhat offset with the fact that this unit has wi-fi connectivity and you can download an app that gives you some of this information on your smart phone. There actually are 3 lights on the front that provide some information, but they are not labeled and it was quite a while before I realized what they meant. Basically, they represent error, run or pause, and completed cycle. The completed cycle light self-cancels when you open the door. I wish there was an option that made it a user cancelled indicator, because if I open the door to assist the drying process then no one else knows that they are clean. The solution for this was to put a magnetic label on the dishwasher that I can manually set to show if the dishes are clean or dirty (but I really shouldn't have to do that with an $800 dishwasher). The programming for this dishwasher seems poor to me. There are a lot of choices, but it's complicated enough that you have to refer to the manual to try to sort them all out. Some of the buttons will toggle between 2 different cycles, but there is no indication of which one you have chosen other than to look at the countdown timer as a clue. There are add on features, but not all the extras work with every cycle, so again you have to refer to the manual to see what will work. For instance, I have wanted to run the “half load” add on to wash only the upper or lower rack, but that is not available with the “Express” setting that I normally use. Finally, they really didn't design this unit for anyone who does any pre-cleaning with their dishes. Having been around for a while I realize that pre-cleaning is the best way to get clean dishes and not have food sprayed off of one dish only to land on another. Fortunately, they did provide one mode (Express) that seems to work well for my normal (pre-washed) needs, and it only runs about ½ hour. All the other modes run well over an hour, up to several hours which seems just too long. Part of that has to do with the sensing portion of the wash cycle where the dishwasher tries to determine how dirty your dishes are.I have had this unit for almost 2 years and had little issue other than a couple of times (once I got the drying issue resolved). Once after putting my dishes away, I noticed that the soap dispenser was still closed. Another time I noted that there was liquid gel soap running down the door under the dispenser, indicating that the soap dispenser door had somehow opened after the cycle was complete. This will be a huge problem if it persists, and I now try to check after every wash cycle which is a hassle. LG says this can happen if anything blocks the stream of water from the middle sprayer because that is what activates the soap dispenser. I do not think anything was blocking the front, but it's something to keep in mind while loading. Lastly, there is an issue with the middle rack in that it can be finicky in its connection at the back when pushing it in. This will be magnified if the 2 sides of the adjustable rack are at different levels, but seems to be somewhat of an issue all the time. If you try closing the door and it will not close, the middle rack is probably not seated fully against the back wall. This is the same rack that contains the sprayer that is activating the soap dispenser, and so I am wondering if it is possible that I was somehow able to close the door without having that back connection fully intact, because that could also explain why the soap dispenser failed to function properly.

I have taken advantage of the rack height adjustability, but only rarely. I really like the top rack and the fact that the left side also has a height adjustment for deeper items. I generally use that adjusted to the deepest setting and almost always have that rack at least half full. The shallow side sees less use, but I like that I can put small items there that I used to always have to hand wash, and don’t worry about them falling through. With all the possible adjustments and efficient placement of the tines I feel like I can get almost twice in this machine as my previous dishwasher. The only real ding I have for the inside design is the handle on the silverware basket. It is wide and interferes with a decent portion of the available space. The good news is that with a butter knife you can depress the clips that hold it in place on each side and remove it. Just a little less convenient not having a handle but gives much more space to load silverware. I never had a silverware basket with slots, but this one works great and I really like the feature. My mom got a new dishwasher after me of a different brand and their silverware basket seems less efficient with the spacing. Another inside feature to mention is the fact that there is no heating element. I have some mixed feelings here. This means that plastic that may fall below won’t get melted on a hot burner, and this is probably more gentle on my dishes and plasticware, so that’s good. They use heat from the wash process that is trapped by your dishes to affect the drying. Initially ALL of my dishes were coming out completely wet. This unit REQUIRES that you use a rinse aid to help with the drying process. Using that does make my China and silverware come out dry, and plastics will have some water but significantly less than before. They do allow you to adjust the amount of rinse aid added, and I have had good luck with the lowest setting. I don’t like the idea of having extra chemicals from the rinse aid added to the surface of my dishes, but this seems to be the current trend and I can at least set the amount to low. LG did include an “extra dry” option, but that adds over an hour to the process and though it’s been a while since I tried using that with no rinse aid, it seems like my dishes were still wet. I would prefer to have some information on the front (especially the timer and maybe a confirmation of the cycle settings) but this is somewhat offset with the fact that this unit has wi-fi connectivity and you can download an app that gives you some of this information on your smart phone. Basically, they represent error, run or pause, and completed cycle. The completed cycle light self-cancels when you open the door. Some of the buttons will toggle between 2 different cycles, but there is no indication of which one you have chosen other than to look at the countdown timer as a clue. There are add on features, but not all the extras work with every cycle, so again you have to refer to the manual to see what will work. For instance, I have wanted to run the “half load” add on to wash only the upper or lower rack, but that is not available with the “Express” setting that I normally use. Having been around for a while I realize that pre-cleaning is the best way to get clean dishes and not have food sprayed off of one dish only to land on another. Fortunately, they did provide one mode (Express) that seems to work well for my normal (pre-washed) needs, and it only runs about ½ hour. All the other modes run well over an hour, up to several hours which seems just too long. Part of that has to do with the sensing portion of the wash cycle where the dishwasher tries to determine how dirty your dishes are.I have had this unit for almost 2 years and had little issue other than a couple of times (once I got the drying issue resolved). Once after putting my dishes away, I noticed that the soap dispenser was still closed. Another time I noted that there was liquid gel soap running down the door under the dispenser, indicating that the soap dispenser door had somehow opened after the cycle was complete. This will be a huge problem if it persists, and I now try to check after every wash cycle which is a hassle. LG says this can happen if anything blocks the stream of water from the middle sprayer because that is what activates the soap dispenser. I do not think anything was blocking the front, but it’s something to keep in mind while loading. Lastly, there is an issue with the middle rack in that it can be finicky in its connection at the back when pushing it in. This will be magnified if the 2 sides of the adjustable rack are at different levels, but seems to be somewhat of an issue all the time. If you try closing the door and it will not close, the middle rack is probably not seated fully against the back wall. This is the same rack that contains the sprayer that is activating the soap dispenser, and so I am wondering if it is possible that I was somehow able to close the door without having that back connection fully intact, because that could also explain why the soap dispenser failed to function properly.

Starting with the inside, this may be the best designed interior I have seen. The tines that hold plates and bowls are very well spaced, and they ALL are adjustable so that they can be lowered out of the way depending on what you happen to be washing. The adjustable heigh middle rack has fold out cup racks for keeping stemware in place. Just make sure that both sides of the rack are adjusted to the same height so that the water connection at the back attaches properly when you push the rack in. The middle height setting is generally perfect for me, allowing my flexible cutting boards on the bottom to clear the middle spray arm, while letting me put taller glassware in the middle rack. I have taken advantage of the rack height adjustability, but only rarely. I really like the top rack and the fact that the left side also has a height adjustment for deeper items. I generally use that adjusted to the deepest setting and almost always have that rack at least half full. The shallow side sees less use, but I like that I can put small items there that I used to always have to hand wash, and don't worry about them falling through. With all the possible adjustments and efficient placement of the tines I feel like I can get almost twice in this machine as my previous dishwasher. The only real ding I have for the inside design is the handle on the silverware basket. It is wide and interferes with a decent portion of the available space. The good news is that with a butter knife you can depress the clips that hold it in place on each side and remove it. Just a little less convenient not having a handle but gives much more space to load silverware. I never had a silverware basket with slots, but this one works great and I really like the feature. My mom got a new dishwasher after me of a different brand and their silverware basket seems less efficient with the spacing. Another inside feature to mention is the fact that there is no heating element. I have some mixed feelings here. This means that plastic that may fall below won't get melted on a hot burner, and this is probably more gentle on my dishes and plasticware, so that's good. They use heat from the wash process that is trapped by your dishes to affect the drying. Initially ALL of my dishes were coming out completely wet. This unit REQUIRES that you use a rinse aid to help with the drying process. Using that does make my China and silverware come out dry, and plastics will have some water but significantly less than before. They do allow you to adjust the amount of rinse aid added, and I have had good luck with the lowest setting. I don't like the idea of having extra chemicals from the rinse aid added to the surface of my dishes, but this seems to be the current trend and I can at least set the amount to low. Cascade rinse aid says that if it gets in your mouth you should rinse your mouth, drink a glass of water and call poison control. LG did include an “extra dry” option, but that adds over an hour to the process and though it's been a while since I tried using that with no rinse aid, it seems like my dishes were still wet. I do use the “night dry” which uses a fan to assist with drying once the wash is complete, but doesn't change the run time. It simply operates for a while after the run time has ended. Opening the door during “night dry” cancels any additional fan time.Now for the outside. The appearance is fine. It's pretty plain. The controls are on top rather than the front, which I have mixed feelings about. They are easy access while the door is open and give a sleek appearance with the door closed, but that means that when in use you have no idea what program was selected or how much time is left on the cycle since the countdown timer is also located on top. I would prefer to have some information on the front (especially the timer and maybe a confirmation of the cycle settings) but this is somewhat offset with the fact that this unit has wi-fi connectivity and you can download an app that gives you some of this information on your smart phone. There actually are 3 lights on the front that provide some information, but they are not labeled and it was quite a while before I realized what they meant. Basically, they represent error, run or pause, and completed cycle. The completed cycle light self-cancels when you open the door. I wish there was an option that made it a user cancelled indicator, because if I open the door to assist the drying process then no one else knows that they are clean. The solution for this was to put a magnetic label on the dishwasher that I can manually set to show if the dishes are clean or dirty (but I really shouldn't have to do that with an $800 dishwasher). The programming for this dishwasher seems poor to me. There are a lot of choices, but it's complicated enough that you have to refer to the manual to try to sort them all out. Some of the buttons will toggle between 2 different cycles, but there is no indication of which one you have chosen other than to look at the countdown timer as a clue. There are add on features, but not all the extras work with every cycle, so again you have to refer to the manual to see what will work. For instance, I have wanted to run the “half load” add on to wash only the upper or lower rack, but that is not available with the “Express” setting that I normally use. Finally, they really didn't design this unit for anyone who does any pre-cleaning with their dishes. Having been around for a while I realize that pre-cleaning is the best way to get clean dishes and not have food sprayed off of one dish only to land on another. Fortunately, they did provide one mode (Express) that seems to work well for my normal (pre-washed) needs, and it only runs about ½ hour. All the other modes run well over an hour, up to several hours which seems just too long. Part of that has to do with the sensing portion of the wash cycle where the dishwasher tries to determine how dirty your dishes are.I have had this unit for almost 2 years and had little issue other than a couple of times (once I got the drying issue resolved). Once after putting my dishes away, I noticed that the soap dispenser was still closed. Another time I noted that there was liquid gel soap running down the door under the dispenser, indicating that the soap dispenser door had somehow opened after the cycle was complete. This will be a huge problem if it persists, and I now try to check after every wash cycle which is a hassle. LG says this can happen if anything blocks the stream of water from the middle sprayer because that is what activates the soap dispenser. I do not think anything was blocking the front, but it's something to keep in mind while loading. Lastly, there is an issue with the middle rack in that it can be finicky in its connection at the back when pushing it in. This will be magnified if the 2 sides of the adjustable rack are at different levels, but seems to be somewhat of an issue all the time. If you try closing the door and it will not close, the middle rack is probably not seated fully against the back wall. This is the same rack that contains the sprayer that is activating the soap dispenser, and so I am wondering if it is possible that I was somehow able to close the door without having that back connection fully intact, because that could also explain why the soap dispenser failed to function properly.

I really do not know how this thing will go. My hope is all time low. Sentence (English): (This review was collected as part of a promotion.)
Comments (English): [ Quiet, Great size and Super clean ] || ---------------- || (This review was collected as part of a promotion.) Bought this unit after having a very good Bosch unit. Must say . this Kitchen Aid is ultra quiet and does a great job of cleaning and drying. I read lots of poor reviews, first, before finally choosing my Kitchen Aid unit. Most common complaint was poor drying. I have found this unit dries dishes with far less streaking than my previous dishwasher ( and we live in an area with very hard water). Also, I love the interior size and prong spacing as well. Despite this dishwasher being a 24" wide unit, as was our previous unit, this Kitchen Aid just seems bigger. It can take a bigger load of dishes and cutlery than our previous unit. And the cutlery basket has a very unique lid/top that you can place cutlery standing through a grid -easy to load and unload.

Sentence (English): So far I love the performance of my 800-series dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ 800 Series Dishwasher - great but not perfect ] || ---------------- || So far I love the performance of my 800-series dishwasher. It cleans very well and is famously quiet. Although I'm an engineer, I've yet to figure out how to use the fold-down wine-glass holding flaps :-) . Also, I am quite disappointed that this model does not have a delay start feature. Although Pg 20, Section 12.5 in the owner's manual indicates that a delay start can be set in Home Connect, but apparently that's not true (as confirmed in a call with BOSCH Customer Support today). It seems I have to set up a start time in "My Schedule", then go back in and delete the scheduled setting afterward. All I want is the ability to set a one-time delayed start -- for example when the temperature is to be in the teens and I want the dishwasher to run at 2am to circulate warm water through the pipes. I had ordered a Bosch model that had a delay start feature on the control panel (in increments of 1 hour up to 24 hours), but that model wasn't available so an "upgrade" was substituted.

Compared to bottle dishwashers, the high and low temperatures are only 5 degrees different, so I think it's a good choice. The clean white exterior is so pretty. If that's too difficult, just search for the instructions on YouTube! As soon as I got home, I bought a 7.3L tub from Daiso and tried it out. It was more than enough! I figured that level of water flow was understandable. I'll use it well!

Sentence (English): Samsung Electronics BESPOKE Countertop Dishwasher, 6-Place capacity.
Comments (English): Samsung Electronics BESPOKE Countertop Dishwasher, 6-Place Capacity. The color is White. As a working mom, juggling work, housework, and childcare was so exhausting that I decided to make things a little easier and hired a dishwasher to help me out. I had heard that "the bigger, the better" when it comes to dishwashers, so I agonized over how many places to buy, ranging from 3-place to 14-place capacity. However, since I currently live in a rented apartment, I ruled out built-in models, meaning a very large one wouldn't work. Honestly, my home is small, and renovating the kitchen cabinets to purchase one was out of the question. While looking for freestanding or countertop models and considering a few options, I came across the Samsung BESPOKE dishwasher, which is a 6-place capacity that doesn't require a built-in installation. I had heard that "the bigger, the better" when it comes to dishwashers, so I agonized over how many places to buy, ranging from 3-place to 14-place capacity. However, since I currently live in a rented apartment, I ruled out built-in models, meaning a very large one wouldn't work. Honestly, my home is small, and renovating the kitchen cabinets to purchase one was out of the question. While looking for freestanding or countertop models and considering a few options, I came across the Samsung BESPOKE dishwasher, which is a 6-place capacity that doesn't require a built-in installation. Even when comparing it to 6-place capacity models from various other brands, this one looked the prettiest. Department stores mostly displayed large-capacity models, so it was difficult to gauge the size of a 6-place capacity dishwasher. I purchased it after checking reviews and measuring the dimensions to see if it would fit in my home. It features a dual water jet system with upper and lower wings, ensuring a thorough cleaning. The cycles include Standard, Powerful, Eco, and Quick. There is also a drum sterilization mode for internal cleaning, which you only need to run about once a month. While it says you can add dishes mid-wash, I generally don't prefer doing that frequently, so it's best to load everything as much as possible before starting. Once the washing cycle is finished, the door opens automatically to allow the dishes to air dry cleanly. It can easily handle a meal for a family of three. Those who need to wash a large volume of dishes should consider increasing the capacity, but I don't think I need a bigger one (I've heard many people say that larger models end up accumulating dishes for several days). It is best to wash dishes immediately after eating. The noise level isn't very loud; while perception varies, I don't mind it if I run it before bed and enter my room. Since it works so hard to clean, it would probably feel strange if it were completely silent. The installation technician called the evening before to schedule the time, and installed it the very next day. They were very kind. It seems all the Samsung Rocket Installation technicians in my area are friendly. They were kind last time too, just like with the washing machine! Anyway, they explained everything well and even gave me a detergent discount coupon before leaving! I also purchased detergent. It has been almost a month since I started using it. Honestly, I regret not buying it sooner. I should have bought it earlier! Hesitation only delays things. When I put in items with completely dried-up rice grains, they didn't come off completely, so I think you should pre-wash those slightly before putting them in. Sentence (English): This dishwasher is replacing my 12+ year old Maytag.
Comments (English): This dishwasher is replacing my 12+ year old Maytag. I installed it myself and made the following observations. This dishwasher is very light at 66 LBS. I could easily lift it up while the Maytag it replaced was over 100 LBS. Plastic is abundant in this unit and it's not necessarily a bad thing. I was impressed with it's quality build with only one exception that I will talk about later. When I put it on it's side to connect a hose pur the instructions water leaked out discharge outlet. That impressed me because it tells me they tested it before sending it to the customer. They either ran it through a test cycle or pressure tested it for leaks. They claim to do 480 quality tests. Very impressive but it's expected from this brand dishwasher. Besides the quality I liked the customization I can do of the wash cycles through the WIFI connection. The only negative was the silverware holder. It is flimsy and falls over. I decided to replace it with my old Maytag silverware holder.

Sentence (English): Acquired the unit for the beach house.
Comments (English): [ A good solid value ] || ---------------- || Acquired the unit for the beach house. I had a great delivery and installation. Everything needed came with the dishwasher. It's a simple dishwasher and I'm still an old-school fan of the front-mounted controls. The dishes come out clean and dry and the 1-hour quick wash does a decent job when in a hurry. I was actually impressed by a big load where I used the steam pre-wash, it removed baked-on grit that I usually would have hand-washed. I just had to put it to the test and it did a good job. I'm a little surprised as to what accumulates in the filter basket. I thought the disposal mechanism would avoid that. However, the filter basket is easily removed and cleaned. It's not a showpiece but it does a better job at a lower price than my more expensive unit at home. The plastic interior can leave your dishes smelling like plastic at first. I ran a cup of vinegar in a wash and that was no longer noticeable. After a month of use, I'd recommend it to anyone looking for a simple and efficient dishwasher.
